category_title: Low-achieving students who monitor collective synthesis and reference usage to improve community knowledge
student_description: S.18 is a student who demonstrates a strong capacity for community-level monitoring but gets stuck on surface-level quantitative data (e.g., note counts) when using analytics tools. She uniquely requires explicit scaffolding to translate raw numbers into qualitative cognitive opportunities and to focus on collective knowledge-building rather than isolated metrics.

criteria.rationale: Over time, S.18 relies on highly structured prompts to independently monitor and regulate her learning when analyzing tool outputs.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must incorporate the consistent use of structured metacognitive prompts (such as Analysis, Motivation, Problem, Plan) to guide the student's ongoing data reflection.

criteria.rationale: S.18 needs foundational, sustained instruction in idea improvement and collective responsibility to effectively utilize community analytics tools.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must include explicit teaching or norm-setting around collaboration, inquiry, and collective idea improvement.

criteria.rationale: Regular engagement in productive discourse helps S.18 dig deeper and formulate higher levels of conceptualization over the duration of the course.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must establish regular routines for peer dialogue or classroom discourse focused on reflecting on the students' inquiry and digital portfolio work.
